**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
enonce_intro_markdown:
A uniform thin rod $OA$, of mass $m$ and length $6a$ can rotate freely in a fixed vertical plane about a fixed horizontal axis through $O$. A uniform circular disc of mass $12m$ and radius $a$ is clamped to the rod so that its centre $C$ lies on the rod and its plane coincides with the plane in which the rod can rotate.

When $OC = x$,
incertitudes: Question 7 : le disque est dans le plan de rotation, donc son axe de rotation (horizontal, par C) est perpendiculaire à son plan : I = (1/2)(12m)a^2. Le corrigé suppose aussi que les petites oscillations se font autour de la verticale descendante (centre de masse sous O), seul équilibre stable ; le sujet ne le dit pas.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find in terms of $m$, $a$ and $x$ the moment of inertia of the system about the horizontal axis through $O$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Rod** (mass $m$, length $6a$) about an axis through its end $O$, perpendicular to the rod:

$$I_{\text{rod}} = \frac{1}{3}m(6a)^2 = 12ma^2$$

**Disc** (mass $12m$, radius $a$). The plane of the disc is the plane of rotation, so the axis through $C$ parallel to the rotation axis is perpendicular to the disc:

$$I_C = \frac{1}{2}(12m)a^2 = 6ma^2$$

By the parallel axes theorem, about the axis through $O$ (at distance $OC = x$):

$$I_{\text{disc}} = I_C + (12m)x^2 = 6ma^2 + 12mx^2$$

**Total:**

$$I = 12ma^2 + 6ma^2 + 12mx^2 = 18ma^2 + 12mx^2 = 6m\left(3a^2 + 2x^2\right)$$

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that the distance of the centre of mass of the composite body from the point $O$ is $\dfrac{1}{13}(3a + 12x)$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The rod has mass $m$ and its centre of mass is at its midpoint, at distance $3a$ from $O$. The disc has mass $12m$ and its centre of mass is at $C$, at distance $x$ from $O$. Taking moments about $O$ for the composite body of mass $13m$, with $\bar{d}$ the distance of its centre of mass from $O$:

$$13m\,\bar{d} = m(3a) + 12m(x)$$

$$\bar{d} = \frac{3a + 12x}{13} = \frac{1}{13}(3a + 12x)$$

as required.
themes: centre of mass of composite bodies

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that the period, $T$, of small oscillations of the system is given by $$T^2 g(a + 4x) = 8\pi^2\left(3a^2 + 2x^2\right).$$
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $\theta$ be the angle between $OA$ and the downward vertical. The weight of the whole system ($13mg$) acts at the centre of mass, at distance $\bar d = \dfrac{3a + 12x}{13}$ from $O$, so its moment about $O$ is

$$13mg\,\bar d\,\sin\theta = mg(3a + 12x)\sin\theta$$

Equation of motion about the axis through $O$ (restoring moment):

$$I\ddot\theta = -mg(3a + 12x)\sin\theta$$

For small oscillations $\sin\theta \approx \theta$:

$$\ddot\theta = -\frac{mg(3a + 12x)}{6m(3a^2 + 2x^2)}\,\theta = -\frac{g(a + 4x)}{2(3a^2 + 2x^2)}\,\theta$$

This is simple harmonic motion with

$$\omega^2 = \frac{g(a + 4x)}{2(3a^2 + 2x^2)}$$

The period is

$$T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega}\ \Rightarrow\ T^2 = \frac{4\pi^2}{\omega^2} = \frac{8\pi^2(3a^2 + 2x^2)}{g(a + 4x)}$$

$$T^2 g(a + 4x) = 8\pi^2\left(3a^2 + 2x^2\right)$$

as required.
